books.title: The Creative Act
books.author: Rick Rubin
books.description: A generous invitation to notice more, listen closely, and make space for creativity in everyday life. Less a manual for making art, more a way of being in the world.

books.title: Before the Coffee Gets Cold
books.author: Toshikazu Kawaguchi
books.description: In a small Tokyo café, a very particular seat offers the chance to travel back in time. Four visitors discover what can change, and what stays with us, over a cup of coffee.

books.title: The Book of Disquiet
books.author: Fernando Pessoa
books.description: A collection of fragments, observations, and waking dreams from a restless inner life. A book to open anywhere, linger over, and return to throughout the years.

books.title: Braiding Sweetgrass
books.author: Robin Wall Kimmerer
books.note: Learning to listen to the living world.
books.description: Botanist Robin Wall Kimmerer brings Indigenous knowledge into conversation with science, exploring the gifts of the natural world and the responsibilities of receiving them.

books.title: The Architecture of Happiness
books.author: Alain de Botton
books.description: An exploration of how our homes, buildings, and everyday surroundings influence who we are and how we feel. A thoughtful look at the relationship between good design and a good life.

books.title: Small Things Like These
books.author: Claire Keegan
books.note: A small book. A lasting impression.
books.description: In an Irish town at Christmas, a coal merchant faces a choice that unsettles his quiet life. A spare and deeply moving story about courage, kindness, and what we owe one another.

books.title: Piranesi
books.author: Susanna Clarke
books.note: Somewhere between a dream and a world.
books.description: A mysterious house of endless halls, statues, tides, and forgotten memories becomes the entire world of its solitary inhabitant.

books.title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built
books.author: Becky Chambers
books.note: A quiet story about finding enough.
books.description: A tea monk and a robot meet on a moon where humanity has learned to live differently. A gentle story about purpose, rest, and what it means to live a good life.

books.title: The Ocean at the End of the Lane
books.author: Neil Gaiman
books.description: Returning to the place where he grew up, a man remembers an impossible childhood encounter that still seems to ripple beneath the surface of ordinary life.

books.title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
books.author: John Green
books.description: A collection of essays examining the strange, beautiful, ordinary things that make up human life, from sunsets and internet culture to disease and hope.

books.title: On Looking
books.author: Alexandra Horowitz
books.note: The familiar becomes strange when you look closely.
books.description: A series of walks becomes an experiment in perception as different experts reveal the overlooked details hidden within ordinary streets and landscapes.

books.title: The Overstory
books.author: Richard Powers
books.note: There are stories older than us.
books.description: Nine strangers are drawn into stories shaped by trees and forests, gradually discovering a world that operates on a scale far beyond a human lifetime.

books.title: Ways of Seeing
books.author: John Berger
books.description: A compact and influential exploration of how we see paintings, photographs, advertisements, and the world around us—and how those ways of seeing are shaped by culture.

books.title: The Story of Art
books.author: E. H. Gombrich

cover.footer: FROM CAVE PAINTINGS TO MODERN ART

books.note: A lifetime of looking at pictures.
books.description: A sweeping introduction to Western art history, tracing the development of painting, sculpture, and architecture through centuries of changing ideas and techniques.

books.title: Meditations
books.author: Marcus Aurelius
books.description: Personal reflections from a Roman emperor on discipline, mortality, responsibility, perception, and the attempt to live well.

books.title: The Consolations of Philosophy
books.author: Alain de Botton
books.description: Six philosophers become companions for six familiar difficulties: unpopularity, poverty, frustration, inadequacy, heartbreak, and the fear of death.

books.title: Man's Search for Meaning
books.author: Viktor E. Frankl
books.note: What remains when everything else is stripped away.
books.description: Part memoir and part psychological reflection, Frankl examines suffering, purpose, and the human search for meaning through the experience of surviving Nazi concentration camps.

books.title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
books.author: John Green
books.description: Personal essays that move between memory, observation, science, and the small rituals of everyday life.

books.title: Crying in H Mart
books.author: Michelle Zauner
books.description: A memoir of family, food, grief, identity, and the complicated ways we remain connected to people after they are gone.

books.title: A Field Guide to Getting Lost
books.author: Rebecca Solnit
books.note: Not every path needs a destination.
books.description: Meditations on uncertainty, wandering, memory, landscape, and the strange freedom that comes from not knowing exactly where we are going.
